question: At actual funded size after partial targets and hourly trims, how much of the observable parent cash profit at completed 12H closes later disappears?
source: Frozen 1000U VIX-aligned queue, 10% of previous-hour median minute turnover, 1585 parents, 42486.13769U fee-only and 39218.47051U with 5bp extra slippage. Native order-level cash/quantity receipts were not saved, so recover these with the identical VectorBT order book and verify every funded amount and hourly equity against the saved reference.
definition: For each parent add all previously executed signed order cash including fees to its actual remaining signed quantity marked to the current native H1 close. At completed UTC 12H boundaries deduct the taker cost and any scenario slippage of exiting that remaining quantity. A parent peak is the largest of zero, its final realized PnL, and these observed executable-price approximations. Peak minus final PnL is retrospective evidence; sum of peaks is not a portfolio backtest or achievable return. Also report peak-to-final difference conditional on an earlier positive marked gain, without treating the initial zero as a profitable peak.
predeclared_exit: Create a strictly causal shadow signal when a finished 12H close has reached at least two original parent cash risks and its later finished 12H liquidation value is at or below half the earlier peak. Original cash risk equals actual opening notional times original protective stop distance / entry. Trigger only while some real leg remains, preserve native higher-priority opening exits at that hour. A separate funded test is required to measure the effect; never exit at the retrospective peak.
limits: Real native positions and fee schedule; simulated execution model, no historic OKX funding or observed exit depth. Previous history was used for research.
